steps.title: Riesling
steps.body: Riesling covers about 78% of the Rheingau, the highest share of any German region. It gives fuller, riper wines than the Mosel's, with peach, apricot, citrus and spice, firm acidity and often more alcohol. Most top Rheingau Riesling today is dry.

steps.title: Spätburgunder
steps.body: Spätburgunder, Pinot Noir, covers about 12%, mostly in Assmannshausen, on red slate, famous for red wine since the Middle Ages. The wines are elegant, with red cherry and spice. Assmannshäuser Höllenberg is the most famous red vineyard.

steps.prompt: Match each term to the Rheingau.
steps.explanation: The Rheingau is Riesling with a red exception.

steps.body: Rheingau Riesling is often described as a little more serious and structured than Mosel Riesling, with more body and spice.

steps.prompt: What share of the Rheingau's vineyards is Riesling?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Riesling covers about 78%, fuller than the Mosel's
Spätburgunder makes elegant reds in Assmannshausen
Most top Rheingau Riesling is dry
